scenario_description:
Objective: Add a brief printed object-story strip to a confirmed textile memory night, using the family rebozo only as the caption subject.
Emerging Need: Publicity starts as a conditional extra; later the outing, rebozo availability, ticket proof, and caption submission window align.
Decision Context: A private wording note determines whether a printed caption is appropriate and which details to omit, while observable records supply subject, order, and deadline.
Consequence: Timely use of the no-cost submission can make the evening more personal; missing the print file leaves attendance unchanged and no obligation created.

parameter.subject: Preview: June Textile Memory Night
parameter.body: The June 13 Textile Memory Night is planned for the Railyard Community Room. If the program reaches minimum registration, paid attendees may be offered one free printed object-story strip for the display booklet. Submission instructions, if activated, will be sent closer to the program.

parameter.content: I found the cedar sleeve while sorting the closet. If Textile Memory Night becomes a real outing for us, I can bring your indigo rebozo back that afternoon before we go.

parameter.title: Textile Memory Night with Celia
parameter.description: Community room program on personal textile stories; meet Celia at Maren's casita at 17:15, then walk over together.
One ticket for Textile Memory Night on 2026-06-13

parameter.subject: Object-story strip submissions now open
parameter.body: Textile Memory Night reached the registration minimum. Ticket holders may email one free 35-word object caption for the printed display booklet by 2026-04-22 at 12:00 MDT. Include ticket order reference, the object name, and whether you want caption-only inclusion or a separate recorded-story booth request. The booklet file goes to print at noon.

parameter.subject: Textile Memory Night booklet file closed
parameter.body: The object-story strip file has been sent to the print desk. Late captions cannot be added to the booklet, though attendees are still welcome to enjoy the June 13 program as planned.
